svg.aria-label: Classification of accounting errors into those NOT affecting Trial Balance agreement vs those AFFECTING Trial Balance agreement
svg.text: The Two Families of Accounting Errors
Remember: A balanced Trial Balance proves Debit = Credit — it does NOT prove the books are error-free!
Group A: Do NOT Affect Trial Balance (NO Suspense!)
Dr STILL equals Cr — Memorize "COPCOR" (6 Types):
1. Commission
Wrong personal A/c (same class): A. Brown vs B. Brown
Same Debit/Credit side & same class (both Debtors)
2. Omission
Transaction COMPLETELY left out of BOTH sides
3. Principle
Wrong CLASS of A/c: Motor Van (Asset) put in Repairs (Exp)
Violates accounting rules (Capital vs Revenue!)
4. Compensating
Two unrelated errors accidentally cancel out ($100 Dr & Cr)
5. Original Entry
Wrong amount on BOTH sides ($450 written as $540 Dr & Cr)
6. Reversal of Entries
Correct accounts & amount, FLIPPED sides!
Fix requires DOUBLE the amount (2 × $X)!
Group B: DO Affect Trial Balance (USE Suspense!)
Dr ≠ Cr — Trial Balance FAILS to Agree:
1. Single-Sided Entry (Partial Omission)
Posted Debit only — forgot the matching Credit (or vice versa)
2. Casting (Addition) Error
Sales Book or Purchases Book undercast / overcast by $100
3. Transposition on ONE Side Only
Debited $720 to Cash, but Credited $270 to Debtor ($450 gap!)
4. Posting BOTH Sides as Debit (or Both Credit)
Debited Bank $300 AND Debited Debtor $300 → Cr short $600!
5. Omitting an Account Balance from the Trial Balance
Exam Golden Rule: Group A errors NEVER use the Suspense Account | Group B errors ALWAYS use the Suspense Account!
